title: Pre-Analysis — Extension of the Inertial Reference Unit Standard to the Remaining Fleet

ata.title: Attitude and Direction — Inertial Reference Unit

abstract: Cancelled pre-analysis of a proposed revision extending the current production inertial reference unit standard to the aircraft still carrying the original units, closed when the work was merged into the avionics obsolescence programme.

sections.objective: Assess a proposal to bring the remaining aircraft onto the current production inertial reference unit standard in one campaign rather than on attrition, and establish what the campaign would change in the navigation rack documentation and in the alignment procedures that line maintenance works to. The order was raised by the avionics office after the spares organisation reported that the original units were being repaired at a cost approaching the price of the current standard.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed before the order was closed. The rack harness sheet shows the connector keying of the original unit and has never been updated for the current standard, which was found through the unit part number rather than through anything the two documents say. The extended alignment time procedure quotes an alignment budget taken from the original unit's specification and would send line maintenance to a serviceable unit on every cold soaked aircraft. The existing retrofit bulletin cannot absorb a fleet campaign of this size: its effectivity is written aircraft by aircraft and it would have to be superseded rather than revised. None of the three is difficult, and all three are shared with two other avionics standards moving through the same programme.
sections.next_steps: The work order was cancelled and the subject merged into the avionics obsolescence programme, where the same rack, the same harness sheet and the same alignment procedure are already being reworked for two other units. Carrying three separate campaigns against one rack was judged to cost more in documentation churn than the units are worth. The three findings and the fleet position were handed over with the closure and no further analysis was done here.

similarity_seeds: fleet campaign to retire an obsolete navigation unit
inertial alignment time on a cold soaked aircraft

tasks.title: Search navigation rack data referencing the two unit standards
Check the alignment budget quoted in the fault isolation data
Establish the campaign cost against the obsolescence programme

expected_findings.rationale: The avionics bay rack harness sheet still shows the connector keying and the shield termination of the original unit. It was retrieved through the unit part number alone; nothing in the two texts is alike, and a text search for a fleet campaign would never have surfaced a wiring sheet.
expected_findings.resolution: Handed to the obsolescence programme, where the same sheet is already open for two other rack units.

expected_findings.rationale: The extended alignment time procedure quotes an alignment budget from the original unit's specification. The current standard settles faster in the cold and the published threshold would declare a serviceable unit faulty on any cold soaked aircraft, which is where the complaint usually comes from.
expected_findings.resolution: Handed over. The procedure needs a threshold per unit standard whichever campaign eventually carries the change.

expected_findings.rationale: The existing retrofit bulletin is written aircraft by aircraft for attrition replacement. A fleet campaign cannot be expressed in that effectivity structure, so the bulletin would have to be superseded by a campaign bulletin rather than revised.
expected_findings.resolution: Recorded for the obsolescence programme, which will carry one campaign bulletin for the whole rack.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares a cabin zone with the subject and uses the word addressing throughout, which pulls it into the similarity pass on any search about unit identification. It installs and addresses cabin light strips and has no connection to the navigation rack.

type_data.conclusion: Cancelled 2026-06-23. The subject was merged into the avionics obsolescence programme, which is already reworking the same rack, harness sheet and alignment procedure for two other units.
